stack: Next.js 12 pages router + Firebase (Firestore, Auth, Storage, Cloud Functions) + Tailwind v3

capabilities.notes: Ported to TanStack Start + Tailwind v4. All source pages ported: home, bookmarks, explore (trends, people), tweet detail, user profile (with replies/media/likes/followers/following tabs), login, reset-password, 404. Verified in browser: sign-in, feed, compose, like, reply, bookmark, profile, trends, people.

Recreated as Lovable Cloud Postgres tables (profiles, tweets, user_stats, bookmarks, follows) with RLS and GRANTs; tweet-deletion cleanup reimplemented as a DB trigger (normalize-stats equivalent). Demo seed tweets and users imported. No records export was attached, so real user data is still pending.

Replaced with Lovable Cloud auth: email/password sign-up/sign-in/reset with email confirmation on, plus managed Google sign-in wired via the Lovable OAuth helper. Sign-up, sign-in, and username setup verified in browser. Existing users must be re-imported (see records) and will set new passwords on first visit.

Private `images` bucket created; uploads at {userId}/{id}; served through the /api/public/media/{userId}/{id} server route that reads with the service role. Public bucket mode was rejected by workspace policy, so the proxy route keeps the bucket private.

capabilities.capability: cloud function notify-email (nodemailer Gmail to personal inbox)
capabilities.next_action: Personal-only Gmail notification needing Gmail credentials. Can be re-added with Lovable transactional email after a verified sender domain; ask the user if they want it.

capabilities.notes: Reimplemented as a Postgres trigger on tweet delete (removes bookmarks/stats, decrements creator's total_tweets).
Bearer token not migrated (API deprecated for this use). Trends now served by app server routes from curated static data (/api/public/trends/place/{woeid}, /api/public/trends/available).

capabilities.next_action: After preview, request CSV/JSON exports of the Firestore users and tweets collections (with original document IDs and emails) and import them into Lovable Cloud.
Request users export with original IDs and emails; map identities on import. Missing emails/duplicates must be flagged, not merged.

capabilities.notes: App lives at Lovable URLs; no Vercel cutover needed.
